page: Amazon Web Services g7.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for graphics-heavy and parallel processing workloads. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores on an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, maintaining a 1:1 physical core to vCPU ratio without simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 128 GB, supplying 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Graphical and compute acceleration is driven by an onboard NVIDIA Blackwell generation RTX PRO 4500 GPU equipped with 32 GB of VRAM.

The instance includes 930 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, offering low-latency scratch capacity directly attached to the host. Network infrastructure delivers a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps, enabling rapid data ingest and high-speed inter-node communication. From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated core architecture and high GPU memory density provide predictable single-thread execution alongside substantial parallel throughput, reducing CPU contention risks common to hyperthreaded instances. However, the bundling of a single workstation GPU with 32 physical cores means cost efficiency depends heavily on workloads capable of simultaneously leveraging both the dense CPU configuration and GPU acceleration.

Workloads best aligned with the g7.8xlarge include high-fidelity 3D rendering, spatial computing, photogrammetry, real-time video encoding, and AI inference pipelines requiring up to 32 GB of GPU memory. The combination of 100 Gbps networking and local NVMe storage also supports distributed rendering nodes, simulation preprocessing, and cloud-hosted virtual workstation deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services g7.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, targeted at graphics-intensive and compute workloads. The platform incorporates 32 dedicated physical x86_64 cores powered by an Intel processor running at 3.9 GHz, paired with 128 GB of system memory at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 GPU from the Blackwell family equipped with 32 GB of VRAM. The instance includes 930 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for low-latency scratch space and delivers a baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps. With dedicated core execution avoiding hyperthreading contention, this configuration balances workstation-class graphics rendering with high-throughput compute and data ingest. It is configured for professional 3D rendering, video processing pipelines, AI inference workloads, and interactive remote graphical workstations requiring substantial local memory and network capacity.
